references.text: In [ref:Joh 4:3-4|John 4:3-4], Jesus' journey from Judea to Galilee is described, which directly explains the background of verse 47 where the official hears that Jesus has come from Judea to Galilee.
The context in [ref:Joh 4:46|John 4:46] introduces the entire story of the royal official's son and places Jesus in Cana in Galilee, where he had turned water into wine.
In [ref:Joh 4:48|John 4:48], Jesus responds with a rebuke that people will not believe unless they see signs and wonders, which directly answers the man's plea in verse 47 and challenges his faith.
In [ref:Joh 4:50-53|John 4:50-53], Jesus answers the man's prayer and heals his son from a distance, showing that the trusting request made in verse 47 was granted.

In [ref:Matt 8:5-6|Matthew 8:5-6], an officer comes to Jesus and asks him to heal his servant, who is lying at home and seriously ill. The parallel is clear: a man of authority asks Jesus to heal another who is near death.

The Canaanite woman in [ref:Matt 15:22-28|Matthew 15:22-28] urgently begs Jesus to heal her daughter. Here too, a parent comes to Jesus in faith for the sake of their child, and Jesus heals from a distance.

In [ref:Mark 5:23|Mark 5:23], the synagogue leader Jairus earnestly asks Jesus to come and lay hands on his daughter who is near death. Here too, a father asks Jesus to come physically to heal a dying child.

In [ref:Luk 7:2-3|Luke 7:2-3], an officer's servant is seriously ill and near death, and the officer sends messengers to Jesus asking him to come and heal. The parallel to the official who asks Jesus to come down and heal his son is clear.

In [ref:Joh 11:3|John 11:3], Lazarus' sisters send word to Jesus that he is sick – a parallel to the official who seeks out Jesus because his son was near death. Both show faith that Jesus can intervene in sickness.

[ref:Sal 107:19-20|Psalm 107:19-20] describes how people cry out to the Lord in their distress, and he sends his word and heals them. The official's prayer to Jesus for healing reflects this pattern from the Psalms.
